title: Enhancing Multimodal Recommendation via Multimodal Representation Calibration in Spectral Domain

problem.claim: Multimodal recommendation integrates user-item interactions with rich item multimodal features to infer user preferences.

gap.claim: Existing methods largely focus on multimodal item fusion while overlooking modality-specific noise characteristics and inter-modal distribution shifts.

contributions.claim: DAMPS denoises and calibrates multimodal representations in the spectral domain using amplitude and phase spectra.
DAMPS uses an adaptive phase calibrator to address inter-modal phase distribution shifts through phase-offset estimation and adaptive phase rotation.
DAMPS uses amplitude variance-ratio and inter-modal coherence filters to suppress modality-specific or irrelevant noise while preserving prominent and shared information.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present DAMPS as a novel framework for multimodal representation denoising and calibration in the spectral domain.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on five public multimodal recommendation datasets reportedly show consistent recommendation improvements and state-of-the-art results.
The authors report that DAMPS is model-agnostic and flexible enough to integrate with various multimodal recommendation backbones.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal recommendation is presented as a state-of-the-art paradigm for inferring user preferences from interactions and item modalities.
Existing fusion-focused methods may amplify modality-specific noise because they overlook modality characteristics and inter-modal distribution shifts.
DAMPS addresses the issue by denoising and calibrating multimodal representations in the spectral domain.
The method decomposes representations into amplitude and phase spectra and applies phase, amplitude, and coherence filters.
The authors report consistent improvements and state-of-the-art results across five public datasets.

source_observation.claim: Fusion can degrade when modality-specific noise and inter-modal distribution shifts are not explicitly modeled.

interpretation.claim: Multimodal systems may benefit from separating shared signal calibration from modality-specific noise suppression.

application.claim: For multimodal recommendation, inspect modality distributions and consider domain-specific calibration before or during fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that spectral calibration is beneficial for modalities, datasets, or tasks outside the reported setting.

unknowns: Dataset names, evaluation metrics, baseline methods, and numerical gains are not specified.
The abstract does not provide ablations, computational costs, or implementation details.
